lines: Economist Isabella Weber argues on Odd Lots that the global cost-of-living crisis is driven by the extreme price volatility of essentials, which traditional metrics like the Consumer Price Index fail to capture accurately.
Weber suggests that interest rate hikes are counterproductive because they increase the cost of capital for vital supply-side infrastructure projects required to alleviate underlying shortages.

The guest proposes an affordability agenda combining short-term sectoral stabilization, such as utility price caps and negotiated food baskets, with long-term, state-led public infrastructure investments.
The discussion highlights that climate change acts as a core driver of inflation, making the green energy transition an essential prerequisite for achieving long-term price stability.
title: Isabella Weber's Vision for an Affordability Agenda
